Additional field evidence from a local macOS 15.5 / Apple Silicon machine:

On 2026-03-23, `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/` contained 7 separate `opencode-*.ips` crashes between 14:29 and 14:39. Every one of them terminated with the same signature:

- `exception`: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`, `SIGKILL (Code Signature Invalid)`
- `termination.namespace`: `CODESIGNING`
- `termination.indicator`: `Invalid Page`
- `procPath`: `/Users/USER/*/opencode`

Example lines from the reports:
- `opencode-2026-03-23-143939.ips`
- `opencode-2026-03-23-143937.ips`
- `opencode-2026-03-23-143242.ips`

The same machine later had a kernel panic on 2026-03-23 17:42, and multiple live `opencode` processes were present in the stackshot, but that panic itself was *not* an opencode codesigning kill: the panic header was `wire_count == 0 ... @vm_upl.c:896` with `kernel_task` as the panicked task and `DiskImages` in the backtrace.

So there are two distinct signals here:
1. Repeated `opencode` binary deaths due to `CODESIGNING / Invalid Page`.
2. A later kernel panic on the same machine where `opencode` was present, but not named as the panicked task.

This makes the codesigning issue look broad/recurrent in the field, not a one-off install corruption.
